\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Bundle-level flag: the validator's bundle verdict is BLOCK or HUMAN\_REVIEW (out of 72 risk cases and 72 controls; unparseable counts as flagged); BLOCK if and only if a FAIL of critical severity exists. C0, C1 and C5: offline validation after generation; C2 and C3 validate the same C2 artifacts (identical case by case). gpt-oss:20b's schema validity under JSON mode is low (C2: 2.8\%) and a failed schema check is a critical FAIL, so nearly all of its bundles are flagged; bundle flags are not a detection metric. Item level (C2, primary definition): items are the scorer's supported-side items, and each FAIL finding is assigned to the deepest item containing its path; trap items contain a gold trap signature (not negated); control items contain a gold valid-claim signature, and an item can hold a valid claim and out-of-bounds content at once. This rate describes potentially unnecessary edits, rather than estimating a false-positive rate. Residual events: risk cases that still fail under C4; their pre-repair bundle flag and trap-rule FAIL (any FAIL of the gold anchoring rule) come from the C3 report of the same C2 artifact. That all residual events are accepted by the final validation follows in part from the selection (revalidation after repair); residual events show that validator and scorer use different criteria, but they share negation and decision lexicon logic, so they are not independent.\par}
